title: 300k open documents in a 12-hour cutover
prompt: You are the migration Lead for an ECC to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition move. Day one needs Business Partners, Products, stock, 180,000 open sales orders and 120,000 open purchase orders. Some orders are partially processed, the business wants legacy identity preserved, and the technical data window is 12 hours. Design the migration approach, dependency sequence, recovery model and go/no-go evidence. An integration team proposes using APIs for all 300,000 open documents because they expect higher throughput.
expected_points: Start from the day-one business state: migrate required master data, eligible open commitments, stock and opening positions; keep closed executed history outside S/4 unless a specific requirement justifies it.

Confirm the exact Public Edition release and migration object for each family. For current 2608 content, open Sales Order and open Purchase Order migration objects use the staging-table approach, so do not choose one technology for every object.

Build dependency waves: target configuration and number ranges, shared master data and target keys, operational master extensions, open documents, then final stock and financial opening controls before business release.

Treat partially processed documents as a business-state decision. Check the exact migration object and approach, preserve executed delivery, goods-receipt, billing or invoice history where it belongs, and recreate only the supported remaining commitment under an approved rule.

Use Migration Cockpit as the default initial-load path where it fits. Use a released API only for a proven gap or a flow that must survive go-live, and prove API semantics, side effects, duplicate control and recovery first.

Budget the 12-hour window by object and reserve time for transfer, validation, rejected records, stock freeze, reconciliation and decision gates. Throughput must be measured with production-like data, not inferred from synthetic request rate.
Keep a governed source-to-target key map when S/4 generates new identities so dependent objects and later support can resolve legacy references.

Define go/no-go on business evidence: accepted key sets, open quantity and value reconciliation, stock quantity and valuation, subledger or G/L tie-out where relevant, critical process smoke tests, known exceptions and a named decision owner.
follow_up_questions: What would you change if the document load consumes nine of the twelve hours in the last rehearsal?
What if the business insists that every legacy sales-order number must remain the S/4 document number?
What is your last safe stop point if stock is already loaded but open-document reconciliation is still failing?
red_flags: Uses APIs for all objects because they look faster without production-like throughput proof
Migrates complete ECC document history into S/4 by default
Calls the migration ready because every technical request returned success
Runs Sales, Procurement, Inventory and Finance as independent cutovers with no dependency graph

title: Partially delivered sales orders at cutover
prompt: Thirty-five thousand ECC sales orders are still commercially open, but they already have partial delivery or billing history. The business says all of them must be migrated as-is so users see one continuous document flow in S/4. Explain the target-state decision, migration rule and proof you require before cutover.
expected_points: Do not assume an open sales-order migration object can reproduce the full executed ECC document flow. Check the exact migration object, approach and current release restrictions first.
Separate the remaining customer commitment from delivery and billing history that has already been executed in ECC.
Define an explicit eligibility rule for each source order: remaining quantity or value, rejection and completion status, delivery and billing state, date scope and approved exclusions.
Where executed history cannot be represented by the supported migration path, retain that history in the agreed legacy or archive and recreate only the supported remaining commitment in S/4.
Reconcile source remaining quantity and value to the target order, not original historical quantity and value.

Test the migrated order through the next real business steps such as delivery creation, availability or scheduling checks where relevant, PGI and billing, and prove that historical references remain traceable.
Keep legacy order identity as a cross-reference when target numbering changes instead of forcing number preservation without checking target numbering rules.
follow_up_questions: What changes if only one item of a ten-item order was delivered?
What if a billing document was cancelled in ECC but the sales-order item is still open?
How would you answer a business user who says the old document flow must be visible inside S/4?
red_flags: Recreates historical deliveries or billing documents only to make the flow look continuous
Migrates original order quantity instead of the remaining commitment
Assumes every technically open ECC order is eligible
Forces legacy numbering before checking whether the target object supports it

title: Open POs already have GR and invoice history
prompt: Twenty-two thousand purchase orders still have open quantity, but ECC already contains goods receipts or supplier invoices for the same PO items. Procurement wants to migrate the whole PO and Finance wants GR/IR to remain correct. Build the migration decision and reconciliation model.
expected_points: Check the exact current Purchase Order migration object and its approach before defining eligibility; do not generalize from one PO status to all purchasing scenarios.
Separate executed procurement and accounting history from the remaining purchase commitment required in S/4.

Define the source eligibility rule using remaining quantity and value, delivery-completed and final-invoice indicators, account assignment, service or item category and other process-specific state that matters.
Where historical GR or invoice chains cannot be moved by the supported path, keep that executed history in the agreed historical system and recreate only the supported remaining commitment.
Reconcile remaining PO quantity and value together with GR/IR and any open financial items so Logistics and Finance agree on the cutover boundary.
Verify target supplier, product, plant, purchasing organisation, account assignment and tax prerequisites before releasing the PO load.
Run a post-migration business test such as goods receipt and invoice processing on representative migrated POs before go/no-go.
follow_up_questions: What if the PO has quantity still open but the final-invoice indicator is set?
How would you treat a PO item with GR posted but invoice blocked?
Who owns the final decision when Logistics says the PO is correct but Finance still has a GR/IR difference?
red_flags: Copies historical GR and invoice documents only to preserve document flow
Reconciles PO count but not remaining quantity, value or GR/IR
Lets Procurement sign off without Finance on accounting-impacting items
Treats all open POs as one homogeneous migration population

title: The API benchmark looks faster than Migration Cockpit
prompt: A team measures 500 API requests per second with small test payloads and proposes replacing Migration Cockpit with APIs for open-document migration. The same team has not tested production-like pricing, validations, custom fields, target-generated keys, timeouts or retries. Decide what evidence you require and when an API-led path is justified.
expected_points: Treat API selection as a business-interface decision, not a transport benchmark. Confirm that the released operation can create the complete required target state.
Check create and update semantics, custom fields, numbering, child entities, concurrency rules, batch restrictions and business side effects for the exact target release.
Measure end-to-end p50 and p95 throughput with realistic documents and target validation enabled. Include throttling, failed records, retry time and reconciliation in the cutover budget.
Design an execution ledger with stable source identity, target key, attempt number, response class and final reconciled state.
Treat timeout after a create as an uncertain outcome. Query the target using a reliable business identifier before retrying so duplicate business objects are not created.
Do not assume a universal idempotency key or exactly-once behaviour; use receiver capabilities plus migration-side duplicate control.

Prefer Migration Cockpit where a released migration object fits the initial-load state. Choose API-led loading for a proven standard gap or when the same governed business integration must continue after go-live and the measured window still works.
follow_up_questions: What would make you reject the API path even if average throughput is higher?
How do you recover when the HTTP client times out after S/4 may already have created the object?
What changes if the API integration must continue permanently after go-live?
red_flags: Uses requests per second as the only performance measure
Retries every timeout immediately
Assumes HTTP 2xx proves the migrated business state is correct
Chooses an older familiar API without checking the current released interface

title: Stock quantity matches but valuation is off by 1.8m
prompt: The final stock migration shows the expected physical quantities, but inventory valuation and the related financial control are off by 1.8 million in company-code currency. Operations wants to go live because warehouse counts are correct. Diagnose the problem and decide whether the business can be released.
expected_points: Treat quantity, stock state, valuation and financial posting as separate controls that must reconcile together for an accounting-relevant stock migration.
Break the difference down by company code or valuation area, plant, product, stock type, batch or special-stock dimension and currency instead of posting one balancing adjustment.
Check the cut-off and movement freeze first so the source and target populations represent the same business moment.
Verify product valuation prerequisites, price or valuation data, quantity units and any mapping or defaulting that can change value while keeping quantity correct.
Trace whether the difference comes from migration scope, source extraction, transformation, target posting or financial reconciliation before correcting anything.
Do not release go-live with an unexplained material inventory-to-finance difference. Use an explicit threshold and named Finance approval for any accepted residual exception.
After correction, rerun both quantity/value reconciliation and representative operational movements so a financial fix does not hide an inventory-state defect.
follow_up_questions: What if the entire difference comes from one product family with a wrong price mapping?
What if quantities match by plant but not by stock type?
Would you ever use a manual journal entry to close the difference before go-live?
red_flags: Approves go-live because warehouse quantity matches
Posts a balancing journal entry before finding the root cause
Checks only total company-code value and not the dimensions that explain the difference
Changes stock quantities to force financial reconciliation

title: The final delta breaks after the source freeze
prompt: A baseline load was taken two days before go-live. ECC remained active and a final delta was planned after the freeze. During the delta, one batch times out with an unknown target result, then the business reopens ECC for emergency orders. Design the authority, watermark, restart and reconciliation rules from that point.
expected_points: Define system authority explicitly. If ECC is reopened, record the exception window and do not pretend the original freeze still defines a closed source population.
Do not advance the delta watermark until the batch is accepted and reconciled. A transport send or timeout is not completion evidence.
Classify the timed-out batch as an uncertain outcome and determine which target objects were actually created before retrying.
Capture emergency source changes with a new controlled delta or approved manual transition path; otherwise the source and target populations will diverge silently.
Use stable source identity and source-to-target key mapping so repeated extraction or replay does not create duplicate target objects.
Recalculate source control totals and target reconciliation after the reopened period, including counts, quantities and values relevant to the object.
Escalate the schedule impact against the last safe stop point and go/no-go criteria instead of hiding the reopened-source event as an operational detail.
follow_up_questions: Who has authority to reopen the legacy system after the formal freeze?
What if the emergency sales orders are already confirmed to customers?
How do you prove that the uncertain batch did not create duplicates?
red_flags: Advances the watermark because the batch was sent
Retries the full batch without checking target state
Allows emergency source processing without a new delta contract
Keeps the original reconciliation totals after the source was reopened
